notes: The R oracle is the Git tree at r_commit, archived with git archive --prefix=NNS/ --format=tar.gz. The NNS_14.2.tar.gz stored upstream predates the zero-total and factor changes. The vendored tools/NNS tree, r_src_tree_hash and tools/NNS_13.0.tar.gz identify the historical snapshot. Native overlays are tracked separately from the accepted NNS-core snapshot.

r14_native_overlays.adaptation: R14 gravity/mode port with std::vector marshalling. CMake replaces only the old central-tendency translation unit; vendor rescale behavior is retained.

R14 multilevel/null-corrected dependence with vector marshalling. R::dhyper and R::pnorm are the ports of R's own nmath routines in src/nns/_rnmath.hpp, so the null expectations match R's bit for bit. Bound explicitly instead of the untouched vendor dependence estimator.

The vendored NNS-core multivariate prediction kernel (src/mreg_predict.cpp, sha256 c98d3fbb93c3165109870cb3d2cc1a55c8cb0fa35770b3ff0204441fd20e1e04) with its Student-t and normal ensemble weights evaluated by R's own nmath dt and dnorm4 (src/nns/_rnmath.hpp) instead of the vendor's lgamma-based closed form, so the weights and predictions match R's NNS_mreg_predict_v2_cpp bit for bit. CMake replaces only the vendor translation unit.

R14 NNS.seas lag scan: SeasComponent and seas_score copied verbatim, scored across lags with nns::parallel_for in place of RcppParallel (each lag writes its own slot, so results never depend on the thread count). Built into the NNS-core library target for its Release optimisation; bound as seas_scores_r14.
R 14.2 zero-total normalisation for scalar and batched nD moments and PM.matrix. Uses the vendored raw moment and matrix kernels.

r_cache_summary.generation: R NNS 14.2. The cache refresh at b184171c supplies the existing entries. The 4a136836 Git tree under R 4.5.0 supplies the new target, factor, dominance and zero-total cases.

r_nmath_ports.notes: dhyper/dbinom_raw/stirlerr/bd0/pow1p and the lower tail of pnorm_both, as called by R::dhyper and R::pnorm in src/NNS_dep.cpp; stirlerr follows the R >= 4.4.0 series cutoffs. dt and dnorm4 are the densities R::dt / Rf_dnorm4 behind src/NNS_mreg_predict.cpp's ensemble weights.
